name: reveal-on-scroll
description: Animates children from a hidden state to a fully revealed one when they first enter the viewport. Built on useInView; defaults to fade + slide-up — the most common 'scroll reveal' pattern.

props.name: from
props.description: Initial AnimateProps. Defaults to { opacity: 0, y: 24 }.

props.name: easing
props.description: Named easing or CSS easing string.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Content revealed when scrolled into view.

examples.title: Feature card reveal
examples.description: Each feature card fades + slides up as the user scrolls past it.

ai.whenToUse: Use to add subtle entrance animations to content below the fold. Standard for marketing landing pages.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use above the fold — those animations should fire on mount, not on scroll. Don't use for sticky elements.
commonMistakes: Setting `once: false` on a long page makes the animation re-fire every scroll-back; users notice and dislike.
Forgetting the `from` is a starting AnimateProps, not a CSS class — it must use motion fields (opacity, x, y, scale).
ai.accessibilityNotes: IntersectionObserver disconnects on unmount. Reduced-motion mode skips the animation; content renders immediately at final state.
